question.text: A mutual fund scheme delivered a return of 14% over the past year. The risk-free rate is 6% and the standard deviation of the fund's returns is 10%. What is the Sharpe ratio of this fund?

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook defines the Sharpe Ratio as (Scheme Return - Risk-Free Return) divided by the Standard Deviation of the scheme. Substituting the given values: (14% - 6%) / 10% = 8% / 10% = 0.80, matching option B. The Trap: Option A (1.40) results from dividing the total scheme return by the standard deviation without subtracting the risk-free rate, which omits the excess-return step. Option C (0.60) and option D (2.00) reflect arithmetic or formula errors that do not follow the defined Sharpe Ratio computation. Note: The workbook explains that a higher Sharpe Ratio indicates better risk-adjusted performance only when comparing schemes that are otherwise comparable; the measure is meaningful for relative comparison rather than as a standalone quality threshold.
